catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class expresses a tool-offset write for a motion platform. cap.device.configure.v1 covers writable resource state, but the upstream set_tool_offset() is a G10 command for a configured tool index and returns no state field; the class is left unbound and this extension carries the inline schema.

notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: wrote a direct Driver over science_jubilee.Machine:Machine instead of the PythonObjectDriver helper, because the motion actions bind catalogue classes with nested object inputs and class outputs and the stop path is the G-code M112 command. The card's read get_position, move_to, home_all and set_tool_offset are covered. NOT COVERED: the tool changer, deck/labware, syringe and pipette tool modules, the crash-detection handler and Machine.reset() (M999 board reset); the U axis is not exposed as a read or a Cartesian action, and Z is homed only through home_all because home_z() prompts on stdin. The harness path (native.py) was never run and the fake is an in-memory stand-in, not a recording; the package was never run on hardware and no human review is claimed. Travel and tool-offset bounds are Limit.operator_required because the clone reads min/max from each machine's config (Machine.py:397-426) and tool offsets shift the coordinates (docs/getting_started/primer.md:72); site-limits.example.json is an illustrative overlay built from docs/gcode/color_mixing_demo_config.g:132-133 and the nominal offsets at lines 150, 163 and 171, not a statement about any unit. The fake start and home positions are placeholders. estop_physical_ref points at the documented tool-ball trigger configuration, not at a verified installation; stop() sends M112, the Duet emergency stop.
